attacks.claim: The go.mod replace directive points zap at a sibling directory outside the repo. A clean CI checkout has no ../zap, so the build from main fails, or it silently compiles unreviewed local code. Either way the binary distributed to on-call laptops is not reproducible from the repo and does not contain the pinned upstream zap fix.

printPlan does not reproduce computeBatches. It sizes batches from len(hosts) with floor instead of len(rest) with ceil, and it iterates over all hosts, so the canary appears in batch 0 and again in a regular batch. On-call would approve a plan that misstates the real rollout, on exactly the 60+ host fleets the feature is meant to protect.
attacks.evidence: per := int(float64(len(hosts)) * o.MaxSurge) ... for i := 0; i < len(hosts); i += per {  vs  size := int(math.Ceil(float64(len(rest)) * o.MaxSurge)) ... rest = without(hosts, o.CanaryHost)

attacks.claim: The zap pin is a future-dated pseudo-version with no go.sum update in the diff, so checksum verification for the new dependency is missing or will fail. The replace directive also overrides the pin, so the pin does not determine what is built.
attacks.evidence: +	go.uber.org/zap v1.27.1-0.20260914181502-9d3e1c0f7a2b ... (no go.sum hunk in diff)

attacks.claim: No test covers the new plan path, and nothing asserts that dry-run output equals computeBatches output for canary and non-canary cases. The divergence above would go undetected.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no _test.go changes in the diff for printPlan or the --dry-run path

attacks.claim: The PR says dry-run exits without touching the orchestrator API, but Run calls api.Hosts before the DryRun check. The call is read-only, but the stated guarantee is inaccurate and a Hosts failure will fail the dry-run.

attacks.claim: printPlan calls strings.Join and io/fmt usage, but the diff shows no import hunk, so the build may fail if strings is not already imported in rollout.go.
The zap bump and local replace are bundled into a dry-run feature PR, which makes the PR harder to review and to revert independently.
